[BBC Business] Household energy bills to hit three-year high as Ofgem announces 4% rise from October
A household using a typical amount of gas and electricity will pay £60 a year more, regulator Ofgem says.

The government is under pressure to support billpayers when domestic energy prices predicted to rise further.

[BBC Business] Reform proposes £30 tax rebate for HMRC phone delays
People on hold to HMRC for more than 30 minutes would get a tax credit under plans announced by Robert Jenrick.

[BBC Business] How parents can save on costs as the new school year starts
From baby banks to supermarket deals, there are many ways parents can ease the back-to-school burden.

[CNBC] Meta settles social media addiction case with California, other states for $16.7 billion

[CNBC] Fed’s preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July

[CNBC] Mark Walter's TWG Global blasts 'attacks,' insists 'no fraud' amid federal probe

[MarketWatch] Home prices in Chicago have jumped more over the past year than in any other U.S. city
Nationally, home prices are rising at a slow pace as housing inventory remains relatively low. But some markets, particularly in the Midwest, are seeing big gains.

[MarketWatch] Meta’s stock rises as the company settles case in social-media addiction trial
The social-media giant agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion as part of the settlement.

[MarketWatch] There’s so much betting against long-term bonds that a turnaround could catch investors off guard, says Citadel Securities
Citadel Securities’ strategist Frank Flight says a bet that appears to be one-sided against long-term bonds could be setting up for a painful unwind.
